# Adjudication Task — Chapter 271

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃271화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|서걱!
  6|
  7|단단하기 이를 데 없는 아이언 골렘의 동체가 순두부처럼 잘려 나간다.
  8|
  9|마력을 머금은 강철이라고 해도 열양지기를 막을 수는 없다.
 10|
 11|창날이 베고 찌르는 곳마다 불의 길이 만들어지며 쇳물이 뚝뚝 떨어졌다.
 12|
 13|띠링. 띠링.
 14|
 15|
 16|
 17|- [Lv.95 아이언 골렘]을 처치하셨습니다!
 18|
 19|- 상당량의 경험치를 얻었습니다!
 20|
 21|- [Lv.95 아이언 골렘]을 처치하셨습니다!
 22|
 23|- 상당량의 경험치를…….
 24|
 25|
 26|
 27|“뭐야, 왜 이렇게 약해?”
 28|
 29|내가 하고서도 얼떨떨할 지경이다.
 30|
 31|아이언 골렘은 상당히, 아니 매우 까다로운 몬스터다. 핵을 파괴하지 않으면 절대 죽지 않은 데다, 파괴력과 내구도가 어마어마하게 높기 때문이다.
 32|
 33|‘트롤을 뛰어넘는 회복력에, 오우거 뺨치는 파괴력.’
 34|
 35|그밖에도 지치지 않는 체력과 마법 내성까지 갖췄다.
 36|
 37|속도가 조금 떨어지는 것이 흠이지만, 수많은 장점을 하나씩 짚어 보면 이걸 흠이라고 할 정도인가 싶다.
 38|
 39|괜히 A급 몬스터인 골렘 중에서도 상위로 취급받는 것이 아니지. 그런데…….
 40|
 41|‘이거 왜 이렇게 쉽냐.’
 42|
 43|후우우웅!
 44|
 45|풍압에 머리카락이 흩날렸다. 정수리를 향해 내리꽂히는 아이언 골렘의 주먹.
 46|
 47|신입 길드원들 사이에서 비명이 터져 나왔다.
 48|
 49|“위험해!”
 50|
 51|쟤는 교육 좀 받아야겠다. 팀원이 위험에 처한 것 같으면 근처에 굴러다니는 짱돌이라도 주워서 견제해 줘야지. 저게 뭐 하는 짓이야.
 52|
 53|‘하긴, 신입이니까.’
 54|
 55|나는 혀를 차며 주먹을 말아쥐었다.
 56|
 57|1초를 반으로 쪼개고 쪼갠 찰나의 순간, 수십 년의 공력이 팔을 따라 내달린다.
 58|
 59|열양지기가 푸른 불꽃으로 화해 주먹에 서렸다.
 60|
 61|그리고…….
 62|
 63|쩌엉!
 64|
 65|그대로 내뻗었다. 주먹과 주먹, 철권(鐵拳)과 멸염신권(滅炎神拳)의 격돌이었다.
 66|
 67|금속음과 함께 지면이 움푹 내려앉고 압축된 공기가 터져 나갔다. 휘몰아치는 바람 사이로 엉거주춤 물러나는 아이언 골렘이 보였다.
 68|
 69|몇 초 전까지만 해도 굳건하게 번쩍이던 한쪽 팔은, 화룡이 집어삼킨 것처럼 쇳물로 변해 떨어지고 있었다.
 70|
 71|- 구워?
 72|
 73|아이언 골렘은 감정이란 것이 존재하지 않는 마법 인형이다.
 74|
 75|그러나 지금, 나는 놈에게서 당혹감이라는 감정을 읽은 것 같았다.
 76|
 77|“어. 당연히 구워야지.”
 78|
 79|땅을 박차고 솟구쳤다.
 80|
 81|쇳빛으로 번들거리는 아이언 골렘의 앞가슴이 눈에 들어온다. 그리고 느껴졌다.
 82|
 83|기(氣)라고는 존재하지 않는 놈의 거대한 동체 속, 가슴 깊은 곳에서 맥동하며 마력을 토해 내는 골렘의 핵이.
 84|
 85|“이 헌터는 공짜로 구워 줍니다.”
 86|
 87|활짝 펼친 손바닥으로 놈의 앞가슴을 후려쳤다. 서늘한 금속은 화염신장(火焰神掌)의 열기에 잡아먹혔다.
 88|
 89|치이이익, 쇳물이 튀며 놈의 가슴에 커다란 구멍이 생겼다. 마력을 공급하던 핵이 힘없이 깨져 나갔다.
 90|
 91|- 그우우우…….
 92|
 93|쿠구구궁!
 94|
 95|핵을 잃은 거대한 동체가 힘을 잃고 조각조각 나며 쓰러진다. 심장이 터진 사람이 숨을 쉴 수 없듯이, 아이언 골렘도 마찬가지다.
 96|
 97|나는 작은 동산처럼 쌓인 쇳덩어리 위에 사뿐히 안착했다.
 98|
 99|“자, 다음.”
100|
101|- 구워어어어!
102|
103|기계음 같은 포효와 함께, 번쩍이는 강철의 물결이 사방에서 덮쳐 왔다.
104|
105|‘이거 다 잡으면 레벨 업 한 번은 하려나.’
106|
107|나는 기대감과 함께 창을 휘둘렀다. 칠 성의 경지에 오른 화룡신창(火龍神槍)이 공기와 소리를 태우며 불의 길을 만들었다.
108|
109|콰아아아!
110|
111|
112|
113|* * *
114|
115|
116|
117|쿠구궁!
118|
119|요란한 굉음과 함께 마지막 아이언 골렘이 허물어졌다.
120|
121|십여 마리의 A급 몬스터를 처리하는 데 걸린 시간은 고작 몇 분 남짓.
122|
123|주위를 둘러보니 모두가 경악한 얼굴로 나를 바라보고 있었다.
124|
125|“이런 미친…….”
126|
127|“봤어요? 방금 봤어요?”
128|
129|“예. 봤어요.”
130|
131|“와, A급 몬스터를 갖고 놀았어. 눈에 보이지도 않아.”
132|
133|“봤다니까.”
134|
135|웅성거리는 신입 길드원들의 머리 위로 목소리가 들려왔다.
136|
137|“레이드 벌써 끝났습니까? 전투 후에는 잔해 수습하고 주위 경계하세요. 길드장님과 송이 씨가 통제해 주시길 바랍니다.”
138|
139|말은 존댓말인데, 어투는 채찍이나 다름없다.
140|
141|사뿐하게 내려앉은 최 팀장의 등장에 어깨를 움찔거린 신입들이 후다닥 할 일을 찾아 흩어졌다.
142|
143|‘가끔 보면 사람이 카리스마가 있단 말이지.’
144|
145|특유의 아우라라고 해야 하나. 저런 것도 다 타고나는 건데.
146|
147|그런 생각을 하고 있을 때, 어느새 눈앞까지 다가온 최 팀장이 굳은 얼굴로 입을 열었다.
148|
149|“진태경 씨. 아까부터 생각했던 건데, 이제는 도저히 못 참겠습니다.”
150|
151|“예.”
152|
153|“그 창, 어디에서 산 겁니까?”
154|
155|“…….”
156|
157|그래, 원래 이런 인간이었지. 잠시 깜빡했다.
158|
159|내 생각을 아는지 모르는지, 최 팀장의 시선은 내 손에 들린 창, 백염(白炎)에 고정되어 있었다.
160|
161|“하나의 예술 작품을 보는 것 같네요. 고전적이지만 아름다운 중국식 디자인, 이거 설마 마정석으로 만든 겁니까?”
162|
163|아니, 만년한철로 만든 건데.
164|
165|물론 사실대로 말해 봤자 골치 아파지니 대충 둘러댔다.
166|
167|“글쎄요. 저도 잘 몰라서.”
168|
169|최 팀장이 탐욕 어린 시선으로 창을 위아래로 훑었다.
170|
171|“외람되지만 혹시 저한테 파실 생각은…….”
172|
173|“없습니다. 안 팔아요.”
174|
175|팔고 싶어도 못 판다. 오직 나만 쓸 수 있는 귀속 아이템이거든. 아이템 정보에도 그렇게 나와 있다.
176|
177|그래서인지 무림과 현대로 각각 구분된 인벤토리에서 유일하게 두 세상을 오고 가는 물건이다.
178|
179|“아아…….”
180|
181|아쉽다는 듯이 입맛을 다신 최 팀장이 화제를 돌렸다.
182|
183|“그나저나 정말 놀랐습니다. 점점 더 강해지시는군요.”
184|
185|나는 농담 반, 진담 반으로 대답했다.
186|
187|“치매 걸린 초절정 고수한테 일 년만 죽어라 배우면 충분해요.”
188|
189|“치매, 뭐라고요?”
190|
191|“초절정 고수요.”
192|
193|“그거 무협 소설에 나오는 단어 아닙니까? 절정 고수, 초절정 고수.”
194|
195|“맞아요. 나중에 은퇴하면 취미 삼아 글이나 하나 써 보려고요. 로그인 무림. 뭐 그런 제목으로다가.”
196|
197|“제목이 별로네요. 대박은 못 치겠습니다.”
198|
199|“사실 쓸 생각도 없어요.”
200|
201|피식 웃은 최 팀장이 입을 열었다.
202|
203|“매번 말씀드리기도 새삼스럽긴 하지만, 진태경 씨를 볼 때마다 가끔 그런 생각이 드네요.”
204|
205|“어떤?”
206|
207|“이 사람이 나와 같은 사람이 맞나, 하는 그런 생각이요.”
208|
209|옅은 갈색빛을 띠는 그의 눈동자가 불그스름하게 달아오르는 듯했다.
210|
211|“만년 F급 헌터가 고작 몇 개월 만에 이렇게까지 강해졌다? 진태경 씨를 직접 보지 못했다면 믿지 않았을 겁니다.”
212|
213|합당한 의심이다.
214|
215|2차 각성자는 흔하지 않지만 그렇다고 아주 희박하다고 할 만큼 적지도 않다.
216|
217|그러나 내 경우에는 일반적인 2차 각성을 월등히 뛰어넘는 경지를 이루었다.
218|
219|더군다나 최 팀장은 그런 내 모습을 가장 가까이서 지켜본 사람이다.
220|
221|‘다른 사람들은 몰라도 최 팀장은 안 속지.’
222|
223|그의 눈에 비친 나는 2차, 3차, 4차 각성자나 다름없다.
224|
225|나는 마른 입술을 핥았다.
226|
227|이건 죽을 때까지 나만 간직해야 하는 비밀이다.
228|
229|혹시라도 새어 나간다면 국정원, 아니 NASA에 끌려가서 평생 실험체로 살게 될지도 몰라.
230|
231|“팀장님. 죄송하지만 그건…….”
232|
233|작게 고개를 저은 최 팀장이 내 말을 잘랐다.
234|
235|“압니다, 진태경 씨에게도 말 못 할 비밀이 있다는 것쯤은. 저도 어떻게 보면 비슷한 입장이라 추궁할 생각은 없고요.”
236|
237|비슷한 입장?
238|
239|머릿속에 의문이 자리 잡기도 전에 그의 말이 이어졌다.
240|
241|“지금껏 유례없는 전대미문의 2차 각성 헌터. 그 정도면 충분하겠죠. 김 집사님도 저와 같은 생각이십니다.”
242|
243|송송이나 임꺽정은 나중에 합류했지만 김 집사는 최 팀장의 곁에서 내 성장을 지켜본 사람이다.
244|
245|안 그래도 이미 F급 헌터의 반란, 기적. 뭐 그런 제목으로 인터넷 뉴스 기사가 쏟아지는 마당에 두 사람이 입을 다물어 준다면 이쯤에서 마무리 지을 수 있다.
246|
247|나는 고개를 꾸벅 숙여 보였다.
248|
249|“감사합니다. 빚을 졌네요.”
250|
251|“별말씀을.”
252|
253|“그런데 한 가지만 물어봐도 되나요?”
254|
255|“뭐든지요.”
256|
257|“이렇게까지 해 주시는 이유가 뭡니까?”
258|
259|“아, 그거요.”
260|
261|최 팀장이 바람 빠지는 소리를 내며 웃었다.
262|
263|“방금 본인 입으로 말씀하셨잖습니까. 빚을 졌다고.”
264|
265|“그랬죠.”
266|
267|“그 빚, 이자까지 쳐서 톡톡히 받아 낼 생각이거든요.”
268|
269|“……?”
270|
271|“그렇게만 알고 계십시오. 그럼.”
272|
273|말을 마친 최 팀장이 돌아서려다 멈칫했다.
274|
275|“아까 말씀하셨던 그 소설, 나중에 쓰시면 한 번 보여 주십시오. 제가 보기보다 소설 읽는 걸 좋아하거든요.”
276|
277|“그럼 제 건 못 읽으시겠네요.”
278|
279|“어째서요?”
280|
281|만약 글을 쓴다면 그건 당신이 좋아하는 소설이 아니라, 내 경험을 옮긴 수필이 될 테니까.
282|
283|말없이 웃는 내 모습에 최 팀장이 고개를 갸웃거렸다.
284|
285|
286|
287|* * *
288|
289|
290|
291|6박 7일로 예정되어 있던 워크숍, 아니 레이드는 고작 사흘 만에 막을 내렸다.
292|
293|혼자 돌아다니며 눈에 띄는 놈들을 족족 때려잡았더니, 더 잡을 몬스터가 없었기 때문이다.
294|
295|“원래는 레이드를 통한 단합 목적이었는데, 이게 이렇게 되네.”
296|
297|황당하다는 듯이 나를 바라보는 송송이의 눈빛을 슬쩍 피했다.
298|
299|게이트 안에 있던 골렘들을 쓸어 버린 것으로도 모자라 보스 몬스터까지 내가 단독 처치했기 때문이다.
300|
301|경험치가 아주 꿀맛이더라.
302|
303|“크흠.”
304|
305|“신입들도 레이드 경험을 쌓아야지. 몬스터만 보면 왜 그렇게 못 나서서 안달이야?”
306|
307|“좋은 게 좋은 거지. 넘어가.”
308|
309|“이보세요, 진태경 씨.”
310|
311|“어허, 넘어갑시다. 송송이 씨.”
312|
313|“그냥 못 넘어가겠다면?”
314|
315|“고백해서 혼내 줄 거야.”
316|
317|“…….”
318|
319|입을 딱 다문 송송이가 겁에 질린 얼굴로 슬금슬금 뒷걸음질 쳤다.
320|
321|목적은 달성했는데 왜 눈물이 날 것 같지.
322|
323|‘하, 사랑했다…….’
324|
325|비련의 남주인공처럼 터벅터벅 걸음을 옮겼다.
326|
327|던전을 빠져나가자 게이트 밖에서 진을 치고 있던 기자들이 일제히 카메라 플래시를 터트렸다.
328|

Right. This was the kind of person he was. I’d forgotten for a moment.

[P77]
Whether he knew what I was thinking or not, Team Leader Choi’s gaze remained fixed on the spear in my hand—White Flame.

[P78]
“It’s like looking at a work of art. A classical yet beautiful Chinese design… Don’t tell me it’s made from Magic Gems?”

[P79]
*No. It’s made from Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron.*

[P80]
Of course, telling him the truth would only cause trouble, so I gave him a vague answer.

[P81]
“I’m not sure. I don’t know much about it myself.”

[P82]
Team Leader Choi’s covetous gaze traveled up and down the spear.

[P83]
“If you don’t mind my asking, would you consider selling it to me…?”

[P84]
“No. It’s not for sale.”

[P85]
Even if I wanted to sell it, I couldn’t. It was a bound Item that only I could use. The Item information said so, too.

[P86]
Perhaps that was why it was the only object capable of traveling between the two separate inventories assigned to Murim and the modern world.

[P87]
“Ah…”

[P88]
Team Leader Choi smacked his lips in disappointment, then changed the subject.

[P89]
“Regardless, I’m truly impressed. You just keep getting stronger.”

[P90]
I answered half-jokingly and half-seriously.

[P91]
“All it takes is training like hell for a year under a Supreme Peak master with dementia.”

[P92]
“Dementia? What did you say?”

[P93]
“A Supreme Peak master.”

[P94]
“Isn’t that a term from wuxia novels? Peak masters and Supreme Peak masters?”

[P95]
“That’s right. I’m thinking of writing a novel as a hobby after I retire. Something like *Murim Login*.”

[P96]
“That title isn’t very good. It won’t be a hit.”

[P97]
“I’m not actually planning to write it.”

[P98]
Team Leader Choi let out a short laugh.

[P99]
“I know I’ve said this before, but sometimes, when I look at you, Mr. Jin Taekyung, a certain thought crosses my mind.”

[P100]
“What thought?”

[P101]
“Whether you and I are truly the same kind of person.”

[P102]
His pale brown eyes seemed to glow faintly red.

[P103]
“A perennial F-rank Hunter becoming this powerful in only a few months? If I hadn’t seen you with my own eyes, I never would have believed it.”

[P104]
It was a reasonable suspicion.

[P105]
Second-awakened Hunters were uncommon, but not so few that they could be considered exceedingly rare.

[P106]
In my case, however, I had reached a realm far beyond any ordinary second awakening.

[P107]
What’s more, Team Leader Choi had watched my transformation from closer than anyone else.

[P108]
*I might fool everyone else, but not Team Leader Choi.*

[P109]
In his eyes, I was practically a second-, third-, and fourth-awakened Hunter all rolled into one.

[P110]
I licked my dry lips.

[P111]
This was a secret I had to take to my grave.

[P112]
If it ever got out, I might be dragged off by the NIS—or no, NASA—and spend the rest of my life as a test subject.

[P113]
“Team Leader. I’m sorry, but that’s…”

[P114]
Team Leader Choi shook his head slightly and cut me off.

[P115]
“I know. I understand that you have secrets you can’t share. In a way, I’m in a similar position, so I have no intention of pressing you.”

[P116]
*A similar position?*

[P117]
Before the question could fully form in my mind, he continued.

[P118]
“An unprecedented second-awakened Hunter unlike anything the world has ever seen. That explanation should be enough, shouldn’t it? Butler Kim feels the same way I do.”

[P119]
Song Song and Im Kkeokjeong had joined us later, but Butler Kim had been at Team Leader Choi’s side, watching me grow.

[P120]
News articles were already pouring out under headlines like *The F-Rank Hunter’s Rebellion* and *A Miracle*. If those two kept their mouths shut, we could leave it at that.

[P121]
I bowed my head.

[P122]
“Thank you. I owe you one.”

[P123]
“Don’t mention it.”

[P124]
“But may I ask you one thing?”

[P125]
“Anything.”

[P126]
“Why are you going this far for me?”

[P127]
“Oh, that?”

[P128]
Team Leader Choi gave a breathy laugh.

[P129]
“You just said it yourself. You owe me.”

[P130]
“I did.”

[P131]
“And I intend to collect that debt in full—with interest.”

[P132]
“…?”

[P133]
“That’s all you need to know. For now.”

[P134]
Team Leader Choi turned to leave, then paused.

[P135]
“That novel you mentioned earlier—if you ever write it, let me read it. I enjoy novels more than you might think.”

[P136]
“Then you won’t be able to read mine.”

[P137]
“Why not?”

[P138]
*Because if I ever write it, it won’t be a novel you’d enjoy. It’ll be an essay about my own experiences.*

[P139]
Team Leader Choi tilted his head at my silent smile.

[P140]
* * *

[P141]
The workshop—or rather, the raid—scheduled to last six nights and seven days ended after only three.

[P142]
I had wandered around alone and beaten down every monster I saw, leaving nothing else to hunt.

[P143]
“It was supposed to be a raid for team bonding, but somehow it turned out like this.”

[P144]
I quietly avoided Song Song’s incredulous stare.

[P145]
Wiping out all the Golems inside the Gate hadn’t been enough. I’d even soloed the boss monster.

[P146]
*That EXP was so damn sweet.*

[P147]
“Ahem.”

[P148]
“The rookies need raid experience, too. Why are you so desperate to jump in every time you see a monster?”

[P149]
“Come on, it all worked out. Let it go.”

[P150]
“Mr. Jin Taekyung.”

[P151]
“Now, now. Let’s just let it go, Miss Song.”

[P152]
“And if I refuse?”

[P153]
“I’ll punish you by confessing my feelings.”

[P154]
“…”

[P155]
Song Song clamped her mouth shut and slowly backed away, terror written across her face.

[P156]
*I got what I wanted, so why do I feel like crying?*

[P157]
*Hah. I loved you…*

[P158]
I trudged away like the tragic male lead of a romance.

[P159]
The moment I exited the dungeon, the reporters camped outside the Gate set off a barrage of camera flashes.

[P160]
I had spent an entire year in Murim, but only a few days had passed in the modern world.

[P161]
It would take more time for all the interest and excitement surrounding me to die down.

[P162]
“Please step back!”

[P163]
“Only authorized personnel are allowed beyond this point!”

[P164]
Only after the guards rushed in and held back the press did I escape the barrage of flashes.

[P165]
Once the shutter sounds finally stopped, the rookie Guild members shouted in unison, their faces flushed with excitement.

[P166]
“Thank you for your hard work!”

[P167]
Their eyes sparkled. Their gazes were filled with admiration and respect as they looked at us.

[P168]
Of course, most of that attention was focused on me.

[P169]
Feeling awkward, I turned toward the founding members. That was when I realized someone was missing.

[P170]
“Where’s Uncle Kkeokjeong?”

[P171]
“Huh? Now that you mention it, he isn’t here.”

[P172]
Team Leader Choi answered.

[P173]
“He spoke to me privately on the way back, then slipped away. Apparently, something came up.”

[P174]
“What could be so urgent that he left without even changing out of his gear?”

[P175]
“It must have been urgent if he left like that.”

[P176]
*What was going on? Had something happened at home?*

[P177]
An uneasy feeling settled in the back of my mind.

[P178]
*Come to think of it, I barely spoke to him after I returned.*

[P179]
I had spent most of the raid operating alone, so I hadn’t had many chances to talk with the others.

[P180]
Looking back, Im Kkeokjeong’s expression had seemed a little dark. At the time, I’d assumed he was simply nervous, but…

[P181]
*Did something serious happen?*

[P182]
Even after I changed out of my gear and everyone went their separate ways, I couldn’t stop thinking about it.

[P183]
I debated calling him for a long time, but in the end, I sent a quick message to the number saved in my contacts. It simply said we should grab a drink sometime soon.

[P184]
He probably had his own problems to deal with, and sticking my nose in where it didn’t belong might be rude.

[P185]
*That should be enough.*

[P186]
I was staring at the stubborn number 1 that refused to disappear when—

[P187]
Bzzzzt.

[P188]
My smartphone vibrated. A phone icon appeared on the screen along with a saved name.

[P189]
It was a name I had entered several months ago and completely forgotten.

[P190]
**Garam Middle School Classmate Park Jihoon**

[P191]
I had run into him by chance on the day I went to buy a house, and he hadn’t contacted me once since.

[P192]
*What could he want?*

[P193]
Mildly curious, I answered the call.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). # Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Right. This was the kind of person he was. I’d forgotten for a moment.

[P77]
Whether he knew what I was thinking or not, Team Leader Choi’s gaze remained fixed on the spear in my hand—White Flame.

[P78]
“It’s like looking at a work of art. A classical yet beautiful Chinese design… Don’t tell me it’s made from Magic Gems?”

[P79]
*No. It’s made from Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron.*

[P80]
Of course, telling him the truth would only cause trouble, so I gave him a vague answer.

[P81]
“I’m not sure. I don’t know much about it myself.”

[P82]
Team Leader Choi’s covetous gaze traveled up and down the spear.

[P83]
“If you don’t mind my asking, would you consider selling it to me…?”

[P84]
“No. It’s not for sale.”

[P85]
Even if I wanted to sell it, I couldn’t. It was a bound Item that only I could use. The Item information said so, too.

[P86]
Perhaps that was why it was the only object capable of traveling between the two separate inventories assigned to Murim and the modern world.

[P87]
“Ah…”

[P88]
Team Leader Choi smacked his lips in disappointment, then changed the subject.

[P89]
“Regardless, I’m truly impressed. You just keep getting stronger.”

[P90]
I answered half-jokingly and half-seriously.

[P91]
“All it takes is training like hell for a year under a Supreme Peak master with dementia.”

[P92]
“Dementia? What did you say?”

[P93]
“A Supreme Peak master.”

[P94]
“Isn’t that a term from wuxia novels? Peak masters and Supreme Peak masters?”

[P95]
“That’s right. I’m thinking of writing a novel as a hobby after I retire. Something like *Murim Login*.”

[P96]
“That title isn’t very good. It won’t be a hit.”

[P97]
“I’m not actually planning to write it.”

[P98]
Team Leader Choi let out a short laugh.

[P99]
“I know I’ve said this before, but sometimes, when I look at you, Mr. Jin Taekyung, a certain thought crosses my mind.”

[P100]
“What thought?”

[P101]
“Whether you and I are truly the same kind of person.”

[P102]
His pale brown eyes seemed to glow faintly red.

[P103]
“A perennial F-rank Hunter becoming this powerful in only a few months? If I hadn’t seen you with my own eyes, I never would have believed it.”

[P104]
It was a reasonable suspicion.

[P105]
Second-awakened Hunters were uncommon, but not so few that they could be considered exceedingly rare.

[P106]
In my case, however, I had reached a realm far beyond any ordinary second awakening.

[P107]
What’s more, Team Leader Choi had watched my transformation from closer than anyone else.

[P108]
*I might fool everyone else, but not Team Leader Choi.*

[P109]
In his eyes, I was practically a second-, third-, and fourth-awakened Hunter all rolled into one.

[P110]
I licked my dry lips.

[P111]
This was a secret I had to take to my grave.

[P112]
If it ever got out, I might be dragged off by the NIS—or no, NASA—and spend the rest of my life as a test subject.

[P113]
“Team Leader. I’m sorry, but that’s…”

[P114]
Team Leader Choi shook his head slightly and cut me off.

[P115]
“I know. I understand that you have secrets you can’t share. In a way, I’m in a similar position, so I have no intention of pressing you.”

[P116]
*A similar position?*

[P117]
Before the question could fully form in my mind, he continued.

[P118]
“An unprecedented second-awakened Hunter unlike anything the world has ever seen. That explanation should be enough, shouldn’t it? Butler Kim feels the same way I do.”

[P119]
Song Song and Im Kkeokjeong had joined us later, but Butler Kim had been at Team Leader Choi’s side, watching me grow.

[P120]
News articles were already pouring out under headlines like *The F-Rank Hunter’s Rebellion* and *A Miracle*. If those two kept their mouths shut, we could leave it at that.

[P121]
I bowed my head.

[P122]
“Thank you. I owe you one.”

[P123]
“Don’t mention it.”

[P124]
“But may I ask you one thing?”

[P125]
“Anything.”

[P126]
“Why are you going this far for me?”

[P127]
“Oh, that?”

[P128]
Team Leader Choi gave a breathy laugh.

[P129]
“You just said it yourself. You owe me.”

[P130]
“I did.”

[P131]
“And I intend to collect that debt in full—with interest.”

[P132]
“…?”

[P133]
“That’s all you need to know. For now.”

[P134]
Team Leader Choi turned to leave, then paused.

[P135]
“That novel you mentioned earlier—if you ever write it, let me read it. I enjoy novels more than you might think.”

[P136]
“Then you won’t be able to read mine.”

[P137]
“Why not?”

[P138]
*Because if I ever write it, it won’t be a novel you’d enjoy. It’ll be an essay about my own experiences.*

[P139]
Team Leader Choi tilted his head at my silent smile.

[P140]
* * *

[P141]
The workshop—or rather, the raid—scheduled to last six nights and seven days ended after only three.

[P142]
I had wandered around alone and beaten down every monster I saw, leaving nothing else to hunt.

[P143]
“It was supposed to be a raid for team bonding, but somehow it turned out like this.”

[P144]
I quietly avoided Song Song’s incredulous stare.

[P145]
Wiping out all the Golems inside the Gate hadn’t been enough. I’d even soloed the boss monster.

[P146]
*That EXP was so damn sweet.*

[P147]
“Ahem.”

[P148]
“The rookies need raid experience, too. Why are you so desperate to jump in every time you see a monster?”

[P149]
“Come on, it all worked out. Let it go.”

[P150]
“Mr. Jin Taekyung.”

[P151]
“Now, now. Let’s just let it go, Miss Song.”

[P152]
“And if I refuse?”

[P153]
“I’ll punish you by confessing my feelings.”

[P154]
“…”

[P155]
Song Song clamped her mouth shut and slowly backed away, terror written across her face.

[P156]
*I got what I wanted, so why do I feel like crying?*

[P157]
*Hah. I loved you…*

[P158]
I trudged away like the tragic male lead of a romance.

[P159]
The moment I exited the dungeon, the reporters camped outside the Gate set off a barrage of camera flashes.

[P160]
I had spent an entire year in Murim, but only a few days had passed in the modern world.

[P161]
It would take more time for all the interest and excitement surrounding me to die down.

[P162]
“Please step back!”

[P163]
“Only authorized personnel are allowed beyond this point!”

[P164]
Only after the guards rushed in and held back the press did I escape the barrage of flashes.

[P165]
Once the shutter sounds finally stopped, the rookie Guild members shouted in unison, their faces flushed with excitement.

[P166]
“Thank you for your hard work!”

[P167]
Their eyes sparkled. Their gazes were filled with admiration and respect as they looked at us.

[P168]
Of course, most of that attention was focused on me.

[P169]
Feeling awkward, I turned toward the founding members. That was when I realized someone was missing.

[P170]
“Where’s Uncle Kkeokjeong?”

[P171]
“Huh? Now that you mention it, he isn’t here.”

[P172]
Team Leader Choi answered.

[P173]
“He spoke to me privately on the way back, then slipped away. Apparently, something came up.”

[P174]
“What could be so urgent that he left without even changing out of his gear?”

[P175]
“It must have been urgent if he left like that.”

[P176]
*What was going on? Had something happened at home?*

[P177]
An uneasy feeling settled in the back of my mind.

[P178]
*Come to think of it, I barely spoke to him after I returned.*

[P179]
I had spent most of the raid operating alone, so I hadn’t had many chances to talk with the others.

[P180]
Looking back, Im Kkeokjeong’s expression had seemed a little dark. At the time, I’d assumed he was simply nervous, but…

[P181]
*Did something serious happen?*

[P182]
Even after I changed out of my gear and everyone went their separate ways, I couldn’t stop thinking about it.

[P183]
I debated calling him for a long time, but in the end, I sent a quick message to the number saved in my contacts. It simply said we should grab a drink sometime soon.

[P184]
He probably had his own problems to deal with, and sticking my nose in where it didn’t belong might be rude.

[P185]
*That should be enough.*

[P186]
I was staring at the stubborn number 1 that refused to disappear when—

[P187]
Bzzzzt.

[P188]
My smartphone vibrated. A phone icon appeared on the screen along with a saved name.

[P189]
It was a name I had entered several months ago and completely forgotten.

[P190]
**Garam Middle School Classmate Park Jihoon**

[P191]
I had run into him by chance on the day I went to buy a house, and he hadn’t contacted me once since.

[P192]
*What could he want?*

[P193]
Mildly curious, I answered the call.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). # Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

[P91]
“All it takes is training like hell for a year under a Supreme Peak master with dementia.”

[P92]
“Dementia? What did you say?”

[P93]
“A Supreme Peak master.”

[P94]
“Isn’t that a term from wuxia novels? Peak masters and Supreme Peak masters?”

[P95]
“That’s right. I’m thinking of writing a novel as a hobby after I retire. Something like *Murim Login*.”

[P96]
“That title isn’t very good. It won’t be a hit.”

[P97]
“I’m not actually planning to write it.”

[P98]
Team Leader Choi let out a short laugh.

[P99]
“I know I’ve said this before, but sometimes, when I look at you, Mr. Jin Taekyung, a certain thought crosses my mind.”

[P100]
“What thought?”

[P101]
“Whether you and I are truly the same kind of person.”

[P102]
His pale brown eyes seemed to glow faintly red.

[P103]
“A perennial F-rank Hunter becoming this powerful in only a few months? If I hadn’t seen you with my own eyes, I never would have believed it.”

[P104]
It was a reasonable suspicion.

[P105]
Second-awakened Hunters were uncommon, but not so few that they could be considered exceedingly rare.

[P106]
In my case, however, I had reached a realm far beyond any ordinary second awakening.

[P107]
What’s more, Team Leader Choi had watched my transformation from closer than anyone else.

[P108]
*I might fool everyone else, but not Team Leader Choi.*

[P109]
In his eyes, I was practically a second-, third-, and fourth-awakened Hunter all rolled into one.

[P110]
I licked my dry lips.

[P111]
This was a secret I had to take to my grave.

[P112]
If it ever got out, I might be dragged off by the NIS—or no, NASA—and spend the rest of my life as a test subject.

[P113]
“Team Leader. I’m sorry, but that’s…”

[P114]
Team Leader Choi shook his head slightly and cut me off.

[P115]
“I know. I understand that you have secrets you can’t share. In a way, I’m in a similar position, so I have no intention of pressing you.”

[P116]
*A similar position?*

[P117]
Before the question could fully form in my mind, he continued.

[P118]
“An unprecedented second-awakened Hunter unlike anything the world has ever seen. That explanation should be enough, shouldn’t it? Butler Kim feels the same way I do.”

[P119]
Song Song and Im Kkeokjeong had joined us later, but Butler Kim had been at Team Leader Choi’s side, watching me grow.

[P120]
News articles were already pouring out under headlines like *The F-Rank Hunter’s Rebellion* and *A Miracle*. If those two kept their mouths shut, we could leave it at that.

[P121]
I bowed my head.

[P122]
“Thank you. I owe you one.”

[P123]
“Don’t mention it.”

[P124]
“But may I ask you one thing?”

[P125]
“Anything.”

[P126]
“Why are you going this far for me?”

[P127]
“Oh, that?”

[P128]
Team Leader Choi gave a breathy laugh.

[P129]
“You just said it yourself. You owe me.”

[P130]
“I did.”

[P131]
“And I intend to collect that debt in full—with interest.”

[P132]
“…?”

[P133]
“That’s all you need to know. For now.”

[P134]

[P135]
“That novel you mentioned earlier—if you ever write it, let me read it. I enjoy novels more than you might think.”

[P136]
“Then you won’t be able to read mine.”

[P137]
“Why not?”

[P138]
*Because if I ever write it, it won’t be a novel you’d enjoy. It’ll be an essay about my own experiences.*

[P139]
Team Leader Choi tilted his head at my silent smile.

[P141]
The workshop—or rather, the raid—scheduled to last six nights and seven days ended after only three.

[P142]
I had wandered around alone and beaten down every monster I saw, leaving nothing else to hunt.

[P143]
“It was supposed to be a raid for team bonding, but somehow it turned out like this.”

[P144]
I quietly avoided Song Song’s incredulous stare.

[P145]
Wiping out all the Golems inside the Gate hadn’t been enough. I’d even soloed the boss monster.

[P146]
*That EXP was so damn sweet.*

[P147]
“Ahem.”

[P148]
“The rookies need raid experience, too. Why are you so desperate to jump in every time you see a monster?”

[P149]
“Come on, it all worked out. Let it go.”

[P150]
“Mr. Jin Taekyung.”

[P151]
“Now, now. Let’s just let it go, Miss Song.”

[P152]
“And if I refuse?”

[P153]

[P154]
“…”

[P155]

[P156]

[P157]
*Hah. I loved you…*

[P158]
I trudged away like the tragic male lead of a romance.

[P159]

[P160]
I had spent an entire year in Murim, but only a few days had passed in the modern world.

[P161]
It would take more time for all the interest and excitement surrounding me to die down.

[P162]
“Please step back!”

[P163]
“Only authorized personnel are allowed beyond this point!”

[P164]

[P165]
Once the shutter sounds finally stopped, the rookie Guild members shouted in unison, their faces flushed with excitement.

[P166]
“Thank you for your hard work!”

[P167]
Their eyes sparkled. Their gazes were filled with admiration and respect as they looked at us.

[P168]
Of course, most of that attention was focused on me.

[P169]
Feeling awkward, I turned toward the founding members. That was when I realized someone was missing.

[P170]
“Where’s Uncle Kkeokjeong?”

[P171]
“Huh? Now that you mention it, he isn’t here.”

[P172]

[P173]
“He spoke to me privately on the way back, then slipped away. Apparently, something came up.”

[P174]
“What could be so urgent that he left without even changing out of his gear?”

[P175]
“It must have been urgent if he left like that.”

[P176]
*What was going on? Had something happened at home?*

[P177]
An uneasy feeling settled in the back of my mind.

[P178]
*Come to think of it, I barely spoke to him after I returned.*

[P179]
I had spent most of the raid operating alone, so I hadn’t had many chances to talk with the others.

[P180]
Looking back, Im Kkeokjeong’s expression had seemed a little dark. At the time, I’d assumed he was simply nervous, but…

[P181]
*Did something serious happen?*

[P182]
Even after I changed out of my gear and everyone went their separate ways, I couldn’t stop thinking about it.

[P183]
I debated calling him for a long time, but in the end, I sent a quick message to the number saved in my contacts. It simply said we should grab a drink sometime soon.

[P184]
He probably had his own problems to deal with, and sticking my nose in where it didn’t belong might be rude.

[P185]
*That should be enough.*

[P186]
I was staring at the stubborn number 1 that refused to disappear when—

[P187]
Bzzzzt.

[P188]
My smartphone vibrated. A phone icon appeared on the screen along with a saved name.

[P189]
It was a name I had entered several months ago and completely forgotten.

[P190]
**Garam Middle School Classmate Park Jihoon**

[P191]
I had run into him by chance on the day I went to buy a house, and he hadn’t contacted me once since.

[P192]
*What could he want?*

[P193]
Mildly curious, I answered the call.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.
